item.title: Gold Bars, Cash Mark Fall of Indonesia’s Top Graft Hunter
item.description: Rows of gold bars, stacks of US and Singapore dollars and seven suitcases found inside a locked safe have become the defining images of one of the biggest scandals to hit Indonesia’s law-enforcement establishment in years.

item.title: MiniMax Shares Slump After JPMorgan Cuts Target Price Further
item.description: MiniMax Group Inc.’s shares plunged, after JPMorgan Chase & Co. slashed the Chinese AI model maker’s price target for the second time in less than a week on value dilution concerns caused by fresh fundraising.

item.title: China Expands Strategic Mineral Toolkit With New Investment Firm
item.description: A new, Beijing-backed mining investment vehicle is aimed at bolstering China’s grip on overseas resources, as the country pushes back against US and European efforts to curb its dominance of the mineral supply chain.

item.title: SBI Funds IPO Anchor Book Draws Capital Group, BlackRock, Goldman, GIC
item.description: The Capital Group Inc., BlackRock Inc., Fidelity Investments and Goldman Sachs Asset Management L.P. are among key investors that participated in the anchor book of SBI Funds Management Ltd., which was subscribed more than 20 times before the company’s initial public offering, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Nippon Paint Offers $8.6 Billion for Akzo Nobel’s Paint Business
item.description: Nippon Paint Holdings Co. has made an offer for Akzo Nobel NV’s decorative paints business in the past month.

item.title: India Inflows at Risk With Foreigners’ Bearish Futures Bets, Mideast Flareup
item.description: Foreign funds’ bearish contracts remain close to last year’s record levels.

item.title: Hyundai Motor Workers Strike Over Bonuses, Robot Job Security
item.description: Hyundai Motor Co. workers began a three-day partial strike on Monday as their union demands bigger bonuses following landmark deals at semiconductor companies, and seek guarantees jobs won’t be lost to AI and robots.

item.title: SK Hynix Shares Slump in Seoul After $26.5 Billion US Debut
item.description: SK Hynix Inc. shares declined in Seoul on Monday after the memory chipmaker’s highly anticipated US trading debut, with traders citing profit taking and a shift to the American depositary receipts as the main drivers.

item.title: US to Increase Mexico Sugar Imports to 1.15 Million Metric Tons
item.description: The US Department of Agriculture estimates it will import as much as 1.15 million metric tons of Mexican sugar in the 2026-2027 period, according to a statement posted on X by Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum.

item.title: Treasury Two-Year Yields Rise to Highest Since 2025 as Oil Jumps
item.description: Treasury two-year yields climbed to their highest level since early 2025 as renewed tensions in Iran pushed up oil prices, fanning speculation that the Federal Reserve will need to raise interest rates to combat inflation.

item.title: Season of Selling to End Philippine Peso Rally, Strategists Say
item.description: The Philippine peso’s relief rally following the initial US-Iran ceasefire is likely to be short-lived as seasonal selling drives the currency to new record lows, strategists say.

item.title: Gold Declines as Renewed US-Iran Strikes Raise Rate-Hike Bets
item.description: Gold declined after the US and Iran exchanged strikes over the weekend, sending energy prices higher and once more raising the prospects for interest-rate hikes to combat inflation.

item.title: Oil Climbs, US Futures Dip on Fresh Iran Strikes: Markets Wrap
item.description: Oil jumped and US equity futures fell after the US launched another round of strikes against Iran, while conflicting claims over the status of the Strait of Hormuz heightened uncertainty.

item.title: Oil Jumps as US and Iran Trade Strikes, Dispute Hormuz Status
item.description: Oil jumped as the US and Iran exchanged fresh strikes, with the sides offering conflicting statements on whether the Strait of Hormuz remains open to shipping.

item.title: US Says It Began Launching More Strikes Against Iran at 5pm ET
item.description: US Central Command forces began launching more strikes against Iran at 5 p.m. ET today, to continue degrading their ability to attack civilian mariners and commercial ships freely transiting the Strait of Hormuz, according to a post on X.

item.description: Andy Burnham, the UK’s presumptive next prime minister, is considering unveiling a bolstered budget later this year as allies and experts seek to persuade him to pursue a land tax, public control of utilities and a more ambitious devolution strategy.

item.title: Traders Grapple With World That’s Good for Dollar, Bad for Bonds
item.description: What’s good for the US dollar isn’t always good for US bonds — but investors are finding ways to work around it.

item.title: NZ Aims to Sign LNG Import Plant Deal Before November Election
item.description: New Zealand plans to sign a contract for its first liquefied natural gas import facility before the November election, with the government betting cheaper global LNG prices in coming years will make the fuel an affordable and reliable backup for renewable electricity.

item.title: Funds Fret Over $4.4 Trillion AI Trio’s Grip on Emerging Markets
item.description: Investors are rotating beyond AI winners in emerging markets, where just three technology stocks worth $4.4 trillion drive an outsized share of returns.

item.title: World Cup Bets on Prediction Markets May Get Tax Edge Over Gambling

item.title: Bangladesh Says Next Deal With IMF Must Ensure Economic Security

item.title: Hormuz Route Open Despite Iran Declaration, Maritime Group Says
item.description: The Strait of Hormuz’s southern route remained open to shipping on Sunday despite Iran declaring the waterway closed as tit-for-tat attacks between the US and Tehran escalated, a maritime advisory group said.

item.title: US, Iran Trade Wave of Attacks as Tehran Says Hormuz Closed
item.description: US forces struck Iran for a third time in a week, prompting retaliatory attacks from Tehran as it declared the Strait of Hormuz would be closed “until further notice.”
